summary: The Food and Drug Administration granted de novo authorization to Virtuoso Surgical’s robotic system for endoscopic surgery to remove bladder tumors, the company said Tuesday. In Virtuoso’s procedure, lesions are removed in one piece in an approach called en bloc resection to obtain tissue for diagnosis of bladder cancer. Two miniaturized robotic arms at the tip of a standard-sized endoscope operate through the urethra, without incisions. The robot, which received breakthrough device designation in September 2025, is the first device in a new FDA classification for electromechanical surgical systems used in endoluminal procedures, where instruments pass through an endoscope into the body.
title: Virtuoso robot wins FDA nod for bladder tumor removal

summary: Labcorp has completed its takeover of accredited specialty laboratory Millennium Health, the company said last week. The takeover, which Labcorp struck last month, is worth $245 million upfront plus up to $130 million in milestone payments. Labcorp bought Millennium to strengthen its toxicology capabilities and expand its geographic footprint.
title: Labcorp completes $375M Millennium Health takeover

summary: Novocure has been denied Food and Drug Administration approval for its device intended to treat non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to the brain. The FDA’s not approvable letter cited uncertainty around the degree of clinical benefit provided by Novocure’s device, Optune Mya, the company said Monday. The system uses low-energy electrical fields to disrupt cancer cells’ ability to grow and divide. The regulator did not raise concerns about the device’s safety profile, Novocure said. The company intends to meet with the FDA to determine if there are other options that would support approval without additional clinical studies.
title: Novocure denied FDA approval for metastatic cancer treatment

summary: The Food and Drug Administration on Friday issued a discussion paper on robotic medical devices with autonomous or remote teleoperation capabilities and is requesting feedback on the systems’ benefits and risks. Autonomous and remote capabilities bring complexity to the benefit-risk consideration, the FDA said. The agency wants input on factors including technical considerations, terminology, risk mitigation and how to develop policy that is responsive to innovation while maintaining device safety and effectiveness. The FDA is asking the robotics community to submit comments on the discussion paper by Jan. 5. Ahead of that deadline, a public workshop to discuss the topics raised in the paper is scheduled for Dec. 2-3.
title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics

summary: Siemens Healthineers said Thursday it will rebrand its in vitro diagnostics business and establish the unit as a standalone organization by mid-2028. The rebranded business, Olyrian Diagnostics, will sell diagnostics for laboratory and point-of-care testing. Clients include Quest Diagnostics, which recently extended its contract by five years. Siemens Healthineers is rebranding its remaining business. Next year, the company will start a three-year transition to rebrand as Healthineers, dropping Siemens from its name. The rebrand coincides with a plan announced late last year for Siemens to give up its controlling stake in Siemens Healthineers. Shareholders will vote about the plan to spin off Siemens Healthineers shares at an annual meeting in February.
title: Siemens Healthineers to rebrand and separate its IVD business
